task.description: Gate the ELIXIR-DEV implementation of ISS-0343 (rescue_missing_schema/1 tolerance for a concurrently-vanished tenant schema in Letflow.EventStore.Registry and Letflow.TenantProvisioning.Backfill) against idiomatic OTP/Elixir usage, supervision integrity, type-safety gaps, and scope creep, per .claude/agents/reviewer.md. Explicit judgment required on SECURITY-REVIEWER's diagnosability note (step-03b): does rescue_missing_schema/1's narrow rescue risk turning a future name-construction/caching bug into a silently-swallowed warning instead of a loud crash, and is that risk acceptable as shipped?
acceptance_criteria: git diff main...HEAD reviewed in full against .claude/agents/reviewer.md's four questions
Checked against docs/anti-patterns.md, in particular the swallow-everything-rescue and fragment/duplication entries
Explicit judgment on SECURITY-REVIEWER's diagnosability note, not deferred or left unresolved
verdict PASS/FAIL with next_action set accordingly

result.summary:
Reviewed git diff main...HEAD (lib/letflow/event_store/registry.ex, lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning/backfill.ex) against the four checklist questions in .claude/agents/reviewer.md, the approved design doc (lib/letflow/design/iss0343-backfill-missing-schema-tolerance.md), and docs/anti-patterns.md.

1) Idiomatic vs. crutch -- N/A / PASS. Neither changed module is a gen_statem or a state-machine implementation; Registry is a plain Ecto-backed data-access module and Backfill is a one-shot reconciliation sweep using Enum.reduce_while/3, which is the idiomatic construct for 'iterate a list, halt early on a real failure, otherwise accumulate' -- no GenServer standing in for a state machine here, so this question doesn't apply to this diff.

2) Supervision -- N/A / PASS. No process, spawn, or supervision tree touched by this diff. Registry and Backfill are called synchronously from whatever process invokes them; no isolation was collapsed, no singleton introduced, nothing here interacts with Letflow.InstanceSupervisor.

3) Type-safety gaps -- checked, none introduced, one already-good practice reinforced. The new :tenant_schema_missing error reason is added to both register_type/2's and get_type/2's @specs (and transitively documented as forwarded by validate_payload/3) rather than left as an undocumented atom a caller could only discover at runtime -- this is exactly the direction item 3 asks for (make invalid/unhandled states representable in the type, not just the runtime behavior). No new class of invalid state was introduced that a struct/Ecto.Enum change would make unrepresentable; the error set is a closed sum type already, this diff extends it correctly. No new docs/issues/ filing needed on this axis.

4) Scope creep -- checked, none found. The fix is exactly as scoped by the approved design: one new private helper (rescue_missing_schema/1) parameterized only over what its three actual call sites need (a zero-arity closure returning `result`), not a generic 'error-mapping middleware' or a behaviour. No new abstraction layer, no macro, nothing built ahead of what ISS-0343 needs. fetch_current_max/2's extraction is the minimum refactor required to wrap the current_max query in the same helper as the other two call sites via a `with` chain -- not gold-plating, it removes duplication that would otherwise exist between the two Repo call sites inside insert_with_monotonicity_check/2.

Anti-patterns check: the 'swallow-everything error handling' pattern this project has flagged before is exactly what rescue_missing_schema/1 avoids -- it rescues Postgrex.Error specifically, pattern-matches the exact `%{postgres: %{code: :undefined_table}}` shape inside the rescue clause, and reraises (`reraise e, __STACKTRACE__`) anything else, including other Postgrex.Error shapes. This is the narrow-rescue discipline the design doc's own section 2.2 calls for and is idiomatic Elixir: matching a subset of an exception's fields inside the rescue clause and reraising the complement, rather than either catching a bare `Postgrex.Error` unconditionally or (worse) `rescue _ ->`. No other anti-patterns.md entry applies (no fragment/1 duplication, no migration/module-name collision, no bookkeeping/timestamp issue in the code itself).

Explicit judgment on SECURITY-REVIEWER's diagnosability note: the concern is that a future bug that makes resolve_schema_name/1 (or its caller) compute a wrong/stale schema_name for the CORRECT tenant -- a typo, a caching bug, a name-construction regression -- would also raise undefined_table and get the same 'expected race, skip and warn' treatment as a genuine concurrent-teardown race, turning what would otherwise be a loud crash into a quiet warning-level skip that could delay detection. I agree this residual risk exists and is real, but I judge it ACCEPTABLE to ship as-is, not a blocker, for three reasons specific to this diff: (a) the rescue is exception-shape-scoped as narrowly as the failure class allows -- Postgrex has no finer-grained signal available to distinguish 'schema legitimately dropped mid-race' from 'schema name was computed wrong' at the SQL layer, both manifest as undefined_table against Postgres with no distinguishing field in the error struct itself, so no narrower rescue clause could close this gap without discarding the fix's whole purpose; (b) the log line is not silent -- Logger.warning/1 fires with the tenant_id on every occurrence, which is real operator-visible signal, just at a lower severity than an unhandled crash; and (c) the fix's actual production trigger (a live tenant-offboarding path racing a reconciliation sweep, per design doc section 2.4) is a real, intended operational scenario this code must tolerate, so a louder failure mode is not available as an alternative without breaking that legitimate case. I record, as SECURITY-REVIEWER also flagged, that this is worth a second look specifically if the warning starts firing for every tenant at once (a fleet-wide pattern would indicate a name-construction bug, not isolated races) -- this is an operational/monitoring concern (whether the log is distinguishable enough to alert on), not a code defect, so I am not filing it as a type-safety issue under docs/issues/ (it isn't a type-representable gap -- there is no @type/struct change that would make 'this undefined_table came from a race vs. a bug' distinguishable, since Postgres itself doesn't carry that distinction). If a future occurrence review wants a stronger signal (e.g. counting consecutive :tenant_schema_missing skips within one run and escalating to Logger.error/1 past some threshold), that would be new scope beyond ISS-0343's diagnosed race and should go through its own design step rather than being bundled into this fix.

No BLOCKER found. mix format/mix compile --warnings-as-errors/mix test (32 passed, targeted backfill_test.exs + registry_test.exs) already run and quoted by ELIXIR-DEV (step-03) and re-confirmed unchanged by SECURITY-REVIEWER's independent diff read (step-03b) -- no code changed since either, so no re-run needed at this gate.
